overview: White follows 1.d3 g6 with 2.g4, the Spike idea: expand on the kingside and use the g-pawn to gain space. Black develops with ...Bg7 and ...d5, challenging the weakened kingside, often with ...h5 to strike at g4. White hopes for a quick Bg2 and e4 centre and an attack, but his king is exposed.

white_ideas.idea: Gain space with g4, Bg2, e4 and Nf3
Keep the bishop on g2 to hit the long diagonal

typical_structures.structure: Pawn on g4 and d3 for White, fianchetto and central pawns for Black

character.notes: The advanced g-pawn creates a weakened king and unbalanced play.

soundness.notes: The early g4 is viewed as inferior and risky.

structure.notes: Flexible as the centre is not yet set.

level.notes: A dubious wing attack; not for beginners.

character.reason: Early g4 leaves both sides chances to attack the exposed king.

gambit.reason: The g-pawn is not attacked so no material is given.

soundness.reason: 2.g4 weakens the kingside with little compensation.

approach.reason: Strong players hardly try the Spike.

plans.reason: White advances flank pawns on the kingside from move two.
